description: We are an engineering/project team of four experts who have come together to develop innovative solutions for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our team consists of a fixed group of members, and this page has been created solely to facilitate the official registration of our members on the platform. We are not accepting any new members from outside the team.
summary: For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we researched spacecraft and robots that have been used to explore Mars. We focused on important missions and robots such as Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, Curiosity, and Ingenuity. We researched the purpose of each mission, how these robots worked, and the technologies they used to explore the Martian surface. We also looked at the discoveries they made about Mars, including its rocks, soil, atmosphere, weather, and water history. By comparing these robots, we learned how Mars exploration has developed over time and how each mission helped scientists understand the planet better. This research helped us learn more about the challenges of exploring Mars and the technologies needed for future missions.
details:
Our project focuses on the robots and spacecraft that have been used to explore Mars. We researched Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, Curiosity, and Ingenuity and examined their missions, technologies, and discoveries. We compared how each robot explored the Martian surface and what kind of information it provided to scientists.

We also looked at how Mars exploration has changed over time, from the early missions to newer technologies such as the Ingenuity helicopter. Through our research, we learned about the challenges of operating robotic vehicles on Mars and how these technologies help scientists study the planet’s surface, atmosphere, rocks, soil, and water history. Our project brings together information about these missions to show the development of Mars exploration and the importance of robotic technology in future space missions.
